name: theta_pointForm
summary: The class sum defining θ, applied to a delta form, is the conjugate kernel at the point h·k; moving k into the datum turns the residue datum into Ψ_Y.

steps.claim: θ of the delta form is the class sum of O.conjKernel g against it, which by classSum_deltaForm (equivariance: conjKernel_equivariant) is O.conjKernel g (h·k) v; moving k ∈ K₀ from the point into the datum (modKernel_mul_Kf_right, under conjugation) leaves an identity of data, proved below.
steps.lean:
(O.harmonicPoly (star v)) g h) := (classSum_deltaForm (O.conjKernel g · |>.toAddMonoidHom)
  (O.conjKernel_equivariant · · ..)).trans ((congrArg star (modKernel_mul_Kf_right ..)).trans (by
  have ⟨s, t⟩ := (exists_reduceAt_mul_incl_eq hY e).choose_spec.2
  set A := Exists.choose _; simp [← map_inv]
  simp [AuxPair.resDetDatum, s, ← inclMatrix_transpose_mul, ← t,
    inv_mul_eq_iff_eq_mul_of_invertible]))

steps.claim: Take the properties s (columns O.incl of k at the chosen places are Y) and t (rows e at the twist places) of the chosen k.
Name k = A and simplify inverses of reductions.

The residue datum O.resDetDatum of k̄⁻¹T (k̄ the reduction of k) is Ψ_Y(T): at the chosen places k̄⁻¹T = I_incl iff T = k̄·I_incl = Y_i (s); at the twist places the rows O.incl of k̄⁻¹T are I_inclᵀ·k̄⁻¹·T = I_eᵀ·T, the rows e of T, because k̄ᵀ·I_e = I_incl (t).
